{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Leroy Milton Kelly''' (May 8, 1914 – February 21, 2002<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130408011137/http://www.death-record.com/l/92540435/Leroy-M-Kelly|title=Death-Record}} for Leroy M Kelly: Holt, Michigan.</ref>) was an American [[mathematician]] whose research primarily concerned [[combinatorial geometry]].<ref name=mathgen>{{mathgenealogy|id=3522|name=Leroy Milton Kelly}}</ref> In 1986 he settled a conjecture of [[Jean-Pierre Serre]] by proving that n points in complex 3-space, not all lying on a plane, determine an [[Sylvester–Gallai theorem|ordinary line]]—that is, a line containing only two of the n points. He taught at [[Michigan State University]].

Kelly received his Ph.D. at the [[University of Missouri]] in 1948, advised by [[Leonard Mascot Blumenthal]].<ref name=mathgen/><ref name=thesis>{{citation|first=Leroy Milton|last=Kelly|year=1948|title=New Properties of Elliptic Space|series=Ph.D. thesis|publisher=[[University of Missouri]]}}.</ref>
